import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Set up the figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Iris Dataset: Species Classification Analysis', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Color palette for species
palette = {'setosa': '#FF6B6B', 'versicolor': '#4ECDC4', 'virginica': '#45B7D1'}

# 1. Scatter plot: Petal Length vs Petal Width (best separating features)
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
for species in df['species'].unique():
    subset = df[df['species'] == species]
    ax1.scatter(subset['petal_length'], subset['petal_width'], 
                label=species.capitalize(), alpha=0.7, s=60, c=palette[species], edgecolors='white')
ax1.set_xlabel('Petal Length (cm)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Petal Width (cm)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Petal Dimensions by Species', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Species', framealpha=0.9)
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 2. Scatter plot: Sepal Length vs Sepal Width
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
for species in df['species'].unique():
    subset = df[df['species'] == species]
    ax2.scatter(subset['sepal_length'], subset['sepal_width'], 
                label=species.capitalize(), alpha=0.7, s=60, c=palette[species], edgecolors='white')
ax2.set_xlabel('Sepal Length (cm)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Sepal Width (cm)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Sepal Dimensions by Species', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.legend(title='Species', framealpha=0.9)
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 3. Box plots for all measurements by species
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
df_melted = df.melt(id_vars=['species'], 
                     value_vars=['sepal_length', 'sepal_width', 'petal_length', 'petal_width'],
                     var_name='Measurement', value_name='Value (cm)')
# Clean up measurement names for display
df_melted['Measurement'] = df_melted['Measurement'].str.replace('_', ' ').str.title()
sns.boxplot(data=df_melted, x='Measurement', y='Value (cm)', hue='species', 
            palette=palette, ax=ax3)
ax3.set_xlabel('Measurement Type', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Value (cm)', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Distribution of Measurements by Species', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend(title='Species', loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9)
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=15)
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# 4. Correlation heatmap for numerical features
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
numeric_cols = ['sepal_length', 'sepal_width', 'petal_length', 'petal_width']
corr_matrix = df[numeric_cols].corr()
# Clean up column names for display
corr_matrix.columns = [col.replace('_', ' ').title() for col in corr_matrix.columns]
corr_matrix.index = [idx.replace('_', ' ').title() for idx in corr_matrix.index]
sns.heatmap(corr_matrix, annot=True, cmap='RdYlBu_r', center=0, 
            square=True, ax=ax4, fmt='.2f', linewidths=0.5,
            cbar_kws={'label': 'Correlation Coefficient'})
ax4.set_title('Feature Correlation Matrix', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
